correctness.rationale: Column and row ideals of the ten-dimensional unital triangular algebra yield leading/trailing principal submatrices; the common size-four and size-one actions cancel. Three-by-three nilpotent Jordan types follow exactly from rank and rank-square. The two discrepancy indicators are proved for every radical input; splitting on whether the middle arrow coefficient vanishes gives six nonzero strata and their exact counts, with the central count by complement. Dimension equality fixes the size-one block difference. Exhaustive direct 10x10-matrix and matrix-power computations agreed on all 64, 729, and 15625 inputs over GF(2), GF(3), GF(5). The finite tests verify only these sizes; the characteristic-free proof proves the theorem for all finite fields.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly classifies a natural left/right regular-similarity invariant for every nilpotent radical element of the elementary first Loewy-length-four upper triangular algebra, with seven distinct signed discrepancy strata, an explicit finite-field mass polynomial and a closed similarity probability. The first possible size-three discrepancy (absent for \(T_3\)) and the first possible size-two discrepancy of magnitude two are exposed; this is neither a single sampled example nor a mere renaming of ordinary Jordan-type counts. The result offers a concrete boundary to the equality phenomenon in shorter cyclic Nakayama models.
